content.text: An ISP that offers a free router upgrade usually benefits from the upgrade more than the customer does. New equipment reduces support calls. The router you return is reconditioned and resold or recycled; the one you kept working was already functional. Before accepting a replacement, check whether the current router's problems have a firmware or configuration solution.
Firmware: keeping the router secure and performing

A router without current router firmware is a security risk. ISP routers update on their own when connected. Third-party routers need manual updates via the admin interface. A router over 5 years old that no longer gets updates from the maker is a real security risk. Replace it, whatever the performance.
Slow Wi-Fi in distant rooms: check the
the device is connecting to. Move far devices to 2.4 GHz band manually. Add a Wi-Fi extender or a mesh Wi-Fi node before replacing the main router.

Dropped connections: check for overheating. Routers placed in enclosed spaces or near heat sources run hotter and become unstable. Place on a hard, flat, ventilated surface away from other electronics.
Router crashes and needs frequent reboots: a factory reset and fresh setup often fixes a corrupted config. Save your settings via the admin interface before resetting.
No firmware updates available for more than 12 months: security risk.
Switching from ADSL to FTTP fibre: incompatible technology; new ONT and router required.
The router does not support WPA3 and the household has high-value data: a security upgrade is justified.

Old routers are WEEE items and must not go in the general waste bin. ISPs are legally required to provide free take-back on request when you accept a replacement. Local council WEEE recycling points accept routers at no charge. Functional routers in good condition can be donated to community organisations via FreeGLe or Buy Nothing groups.

attrs.symptom: ISP saying you need a new router for the upgrade to work

content.text: Ask specifically which technical incompatibility requires the new hardware. Switching from ADSL to FTTP is a genuine incompatibility. Staying on FTTC fibre with a speed upgrade does not require a new router if the existing router handles the current speed.
